report_name: Emperador Ransomware Claims Attack on US Firm A-RMS

threat_actors.name: Emperador
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that conducted a double-extortion attack against A-RMS, a US-based organization. The group publicly claimed the attack on October 25, 2026.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Emperador ransomware payload was deployed to encrypt files on the victim's network to cause disruption and extort the victim.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The attackers exfiltrated a copy of the victim's data to their own infrastructure to use as leverage in a double-extortion scheme.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely deleted backups to inhibit recovery efforts by the victim as part of the final stage of the attack.

attack_patterns.name: System Information Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The use of tools like AdFind was noted for Active Directory reconnaissance to identify critical assets on the victim network.

attack_patterns.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
attack_patterns.description: The use of 'wevtutil.exe cl' was noted as a command-line pattern, indicating the attackers cleared Windows Event Logs to cover their tracks.

malware.name: Emperador Ransomware
malware.description: The proprietary ransomware used by the Emperador group to encrypt files and exfiltrate data in the attack against A-RMS.

tools.name: AdFind
tools.description: AdFind was mentioned as a tool used for Active Directory reconnaissance during ransomware attacks.

identities.name: A-RMS
identities.description: A U.S.-based organization targeted by the Emperador ransomware group in a cyberattack claimed on October 25, 2026.

indicators.name: AdFind Tool Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: AdFind Execution For Active Directory Reconnaissance
id: 2b9c3f1a-8d7e-4b6f-9c1d-0a2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of AdFind, a tool commonly used for Active Directory reconnaissance by ransomware groups.
references:
  - https://www.hookphish.com/blog/ransomware-group-emperador-hits-a-rms/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-25
tags:
  - attack.t1082
  - attack.discovery
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\adfind.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the AdFind tool, which is commonly used for Active Directory reconnaissance in ransomware attacks.

indicators.name: Windows Event Log Clearing with Wevtutil
indicators.pattern:
title: Windows Event Log Cleared with Wevtutil
id: 8e1f2a3b-4c5d-4e6f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of wevtutil.exe to clear system event logs, a common technique used by attackers to cover their tracks.
references:
  - https://www.hookphish.com/blog/ransomware-group-emperador-hits-a-rms/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-25
tags:
  - attack.t1070.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\wevtutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' cl '
  condition: all of selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of 'wevtutil.exe cl' to clear Windows Event Logs, a behavior associated with defense evasion.

relationships.source_name: Windows Event Log Clearing with Wevtutil
